title: The names of the twelve apostles who preached the gospel of Christ and how they died
english: 1. Simon Peter, the foremost of the apostles, as is evident through his letters, preached the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ in Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Bithynia, Italy, Asia, and Illyricum; later, under King Nero in Rome, he was crucified upside down, being worthy to suffer thus, and was buried in Rome three days before the Kalends of July.

2. Andrew, his brother, as those before us have handed down, preached to the Scythians, the Sogdians, the Gorsini, and in the great Sebasteopolis, where the colony of Apsarus is, and the port of Issus, and the Phasis river, where the Ethiopians dwell; he was buried in Patrae of Achaia, having been fastened to a cross by Aegeas, the king of Patrae.

3. James, the son of Zebedee, brother of John the Evangelist, preached the gospel of Christ to the twelve tribes of the Dispersion, but was put to death by the sword under Herod, the tetrarch of the Jews, and was buried there in Judea.

4. John, his brother, preached the gospel of Christ in Asia, but was exiled by the Roman Emperor Trajan to the island of Patmos because of the word of the Lord; while there, he wrote the Gospel according to John and released it through Gaius the host; after the death of Trajan, he returned from the island to Ephesus and was buried there, living until he was ninety years of age by the will of God.
5. Philip the apostle, who was from the village of Bethsaida of Peter and Andrew, preached the gospel in Upper Phrygia; he dies in Hierapolis and is buried there gloriously with his own.

6. Bartholomew the apostle preached the gospel of Christ to the Indians, who are called the Eudaimon; having written the holy Gospel according to Matthew for them in their own dialect, he fell asleep in the great city of Albanopolis in Armenia and was buried there.

7. Thomas the apostle, as the tradition contains, was from the city of Panias in Galilee; he preached the gospel of the Lord to the Parthians and the Medes, and also to the Persians, the Germans, the Hyrcanians, the Indians, the Bactrians, and the Magi, and fell asleep in the city of Calaminus in India.
8. Matthew the Evangelist was from Jerusalem, and there he wrote the gospel of the Lord in the Hebrew dialect and released it to the saints...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
